title: [dynamo] Fix canonicalize_output_graph_node_order dropping inference_mode
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #195518

Fixes #195418

With torch._dynamo.config.canonicalize_output_graph_node_order = True,
compiling a function that uses torch.inference_mode() silently produced
outputs as if inference_mode had never been entered (requires_grad=True,
is_inference=False), with no error or graph break.

Root cause: Dynamo traces inference_mode into call_function nodes on
torch.autograd.grad_mode._enter_inference_mode / _exit_inference_mode.
The canonicalization pass's _is_safe_to_reorder treats non-OpOverload
call_functions as pure unless an impurity check catches them, and
_exit_inference_mode escaped all of them: it is not registered in FX's
_side_effectful_functions (unlike the autocast and set_grad_enabled
equivalents, so is_impure() returned False), its name does not end in
"_", and because it consumes the token produced by the enter node it
also escaped the "no FX Node arguments" heuristic that catches the
enter node. Classified reorderable, it was hoisted above the compute by
Kahn's-algorithm tiebreaking, yielding enter; exit; add -- the compute
ran outside the inference region. The same escape class covers other
token-consuming state functions (_sdpa_kernel, _maybe_exchange_device,
push_dynamic_layer_stack, _vmap_increment_nesting with a SymInt node).

The fix has two halves; either alone fixes the reordering bug, but both
are kept because each has independent value. First, register
_enter_inference_mode/_exit_inference_mode in _side_effectful_functions
(mirroring the autocast precedent), which makes is_impure() truthful
and additionally fixes a latent DCE hazard: eliminate_dead_code()
previously deleted both inference-mode nodes since the exit node has no
users. Second, close the general hole in _is_safe_to_reorder: a
non-OpOverload call_function whose meta carries no Tensor/SymInt/
SymFloat/SymBool in example_value/val is now a barrier. Dynamo and
export attach such a value to every data-producing node and never to
state-only ops, so this covers the whole escape class rather than
special-casing inference_mode; misclassification is only ever
conservative (a false barrier reduces reordering but cannot produce a
wrong order).

Test Plan:

New regression tests: an e2e repro test (verified to fail before the
fix) and unit tests for the new barrier contract:

```
python test/dynamo/test_ctx_manager.py -k test_inference_mode_canonicalize_node_order
python test/dynamo/test_dicts.py -k canonical
```

Targeted suites (the whole Dynamo suite runs with the canonicalize flag
enabled via torch._dynamo.test_case.TestCase, so these exercise the new
heuristic broadly):

```
python test/dynamo/test_ctx_manager.py
python test/dynamo/test_dicts.py
python test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py
python test/dynamo/test_sdpa.py
python test/dynamo/test_streams.py
python test/dynamo/test_deviceguard.py
python test/dynamo/test_export.py
python test/dynamo/test_misc.py -k inference
python test/dynamo/test_misc.py -k grad
python test/dynamo/test_aot_autograd.py -k inference
python test/export/test_export.py -k grad
python -m pytest test/fx/test_dce_pass.py -q
```

All pass (skips/expected-failures match clean HEAD). lintrunner -a is
clean on the changed files.
